newsitem.title: USA: San Jose, Calif., airport unveils expansion plans.
newsitem.headline: San Jose, Calif., airport unveils expansion plans.

text.p: The San Jose International Airport has developed expansion proposals that could cost over $800 million and would be funded, at least in part, with revenue bond, a spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

Cathy Gaskell, airport spokeswoman, said these proposals include plans for airfield projects, terminal expansion and other developments that would help the airport meet projected passenger and cargo growth through 2010.
The airport said it developed three expansion alternatives. The most extensive of these plans would cost an estimated $809 million.
Gaskell said funding would come from federal grants, airport revenues, such as landing and other user fees, and revenue bonds. General tax money would not be used.
Gaskell said the San Jose City Council was expected to select one of the alternatives early next year.
